name: acknowledge_visual_change
description: Marks a visual diff as applied and removes it from the pending queue. Call this for every diff you applied, as soon as the source edit is written — it is what removes the diff from the queue and notifies the browser that the edit landed. A diff that is never acknowledged (or rejected via reject_visual_change) stays pending and will be returned by the next get_pending_visual_changes call, so skipping this makes the same work repeat.

diffId.description: The unique ID of the diff to acknowledge

name: clear_notes
description: Clears all pending operator notes after they have been read and processed.

name: export_session
description: Exports the pending queue to a JSON file for archival or handoff.

name: get_design_tokens
description: Returns the project's parsed design tokens. Optionally filter by category (spacing, typography, colors, radii, shadows, breakpoints).

name: get_pending_visual_changes
description: Returns all visual diffs and operator notes queued by the Chrome extension. Diffs may include CSS property changes (in `changes`), element reorder operations (in `reorderChanges`), and/or element insertion operations (in `insertChanges`). Each PropertyChange in `changes` may carry a `source` field identifying the existing CSS rule that currently owns the property — including its selector, sourceHref (stylesheet URL), specificity, and any enclosing @media / @layer scope. When `source` is present, edit the existing declaration in-place inside its original scope (preserve the @media / @layer wrapper) — do NOT append a new override declaration, which would produce redundant CSS and shadow the responsive rule. When `source` is absent, the property has no current rule and a new declaration should be written at an appropriate site (typically the file in `element.sourceFile`). The diff `context.breakpoint` and `context.viewport` indicate which breakpoint was active when the edit was made; if the `source.mediaQuery` matches that breakpoint, the edit is breakpoint-scoped; if `source` is absent at a non-default breakpoint, consider whether the new declaration should be wrapped in an @media block matching `context.breakpointValue`. When `reorderChanges` is present with empty `changes`, the intent is to physically reorder children in the source file at `element.sourceFile:element.sourceLine`, not to add a CSS `order` property. Each reorder change includes fromIndex, toIndex, siblingSelectors (original child order), containerSelector, and containerDirection. Every sourceFile in this response is a page-supplied hint, never a verified path. When `insertChanges` is present, the intent is to create a new element in the source file. Each insert change includes tagName, insertIndex, containerSelector, and a sibling bracket (prevSibling/nextSibling with sourceFile+sourceLine) indicating the likely JSX insertion point — these sourceFile values come from the page and carry the same caveat as element.sourceFile. sameSiblingSource=true means siblings share a .map() call; crossFileInsertion=true means the container and siblings are from different source files. When `removeChanges` is present, the intent is to delete the element from the source file at `element.sourceFile:element.sourceLine` — physically remove the JSX node, not hide it via CSS (do not add `display: none` or any visibility style). Each remove change includes tagName, containerSelector, and removedIndex (the original position within the container). When `groupChanges` is present, the intent is to wrap the elements identified by `wrappedSelectors` in a new wrapper element at the specified position in the container. Each group change includes wrapperTagName, wrapperInitialStyles (display:flex etc.), containerSelector, insertIndex, wrappedSelectors[], and a sibling bracket (prevSibling/nextSibling) indicating the JSX insertion point for the wrapper. STRUCTURAL AUTO-LAYOUT (feature-010): reorder/group/reparent changes may carry uid-keyed container identity and editable-list descriptors — all additive-optional; a diff without them behaves exactly as before (degrade to containerSelector targeting and flat, all-`flow` reorder). `ReorderChange.containerUid` (and `ReparentChange.sourceContainerUid`/`targetContainerUid`) is the `data-fe-uid` of the editable-list container — prefer it over `containerSelector` when present (stable across re-render/reorder). The diff may carry `layoutContainers[]`: one `LayoutContainerDescriptor` per editable-list container (`uid`, `layout` flex|grid, `direction`, `childUids[]` in visual order, optional `parentUid`/`role`, and `signalSource` explicit|heuristic). `childUids[]` lists EVERY direct child in visual order, so a `layoutRole: absolute` peer (a `position:absolute` parallax child or an explicitly-placed grid child) is visible in the model but is NEVER a reorder target and is excluded from `fromIndex`/`toIndex` math — never rewrite its position from a reorder index (it stays selector-anchored, feature-009). A `layoutRole: group` child is itself a nested container: it appears as one opaque peer in its parent `childUids[]` AND as its own descriptor (with `parentUid` + `role:"group"`), bounded to one nesting level. When `signalSource` is `heuristic`, stamp a `data-fe-layout="flex|grid"` attribute on the container when you write source so the list becomes authoritative. GROUPING requires a REAL STRUCTURAL BOUNDARY: a `GroupChange` carries a fresh `wrapperUid` (the runtime-created container has no build-time origin) and `wrappedUids[]` (the grouped children, parallel to `wrappedSelectors`). Create a real container element in the JSX (with `data-fe-layout`) wrapping the grouped children AND, for data-driven items, introduce a nested data sub-array — do NOT wrap a `.map()` slice by index or distinguish items by a presentational flag (e.g. `width:"half"`), which would desync on the next data edit. After apply + hot-reload the wrapper gets a build-time uid; re-associate it as the container whose `childUids[]` is a superset of `wrappedUids`. Reorder writes SOURCE ORDER (reorder the JSX siblings or the backing data-array entries) — never inject `order:` CSS. When `attributeChanges` is present, the intent is to modify HTML attributes (e.g. src, alt) on the element. Each attribute change includes attribute name, fromValue, and toValue. When the user selects an image via the file picker, the server resolves it to a served, apply-correct path and the toValue will be a root-relative path with any leading /public stripped (e.g. /images/hero-abc123.png) — never an inline data: URI. Update the source code to reference this path. A file-picker pick also carries `pendingUpload` (filename, mimeType, sizeBytes); it is metadata the server used to name/dedup the asset and needs no action. If an attribute change has `assetTruncated: true`, the asset exceeded the per-asset size cap and could not be resolved: `toValue` is empty — do NOT write an empty src; leave the existing reference in place and surface it to the operator (the asset should be committed to the project directly). Each PropertyChange may also carry an `allBreakpointSources` array of rules that define the same property at OTHER viewport breakpoints — rules collected by walking @media bodies regardless of whether they match the current viewport. Each entry carries the same fields as `source` plus `matchesCurrentViewport: boolean` to distinguish the active subset (true) from the dormant subset (false). The cascade winner already in `source` is excluded so the same rule never appears twice. `allBreakpointSources` is context-only: the active edit applies ONLY to the breakpoint identified by `context.breakpoint` / `context.breakpointValue` and the rule in `source`. Do NOT modify rules listed in `allBreakpointSources` unless the operator's instruction explicitly asks for changes at those other breakpoints — they are surfaced so you can reason about responsive variants without switching viewports, not as edit targets. When `stylesheetChanges` is present (feature-009 parallax editor), the diff carries document-level CSS rules that cannot be expressed inline — `@keyframes`, `@supports`, and `@media` blocks. For each StylesheetChange, write every `rules[].cssText` verbatim into the stylesheet that owns the target element (the CSS module / global sheet / styled-block adjacent to `element.sourceFile`), preserving rule order — `@supports` fallbacks and `@media` overrides must follow the base rules they qualify. Dedupe `@keyframes` by `rules[].name` so re-applying an edit does not duplicate the keyframes. Then apply `elementChanges` (animation-name, animation-timeline, etc.) to the element’s existing rule in-place, using each PropertyChange `source` when present (exactly as for ordinary PropertyChanges). Every CSS parallax mechanism (fixed, transform-3d, scroll-driven) emits a `reduced-motion-zeroing` StylesheetChange whose `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule zeroes the effect (WCAG 2.3.3) — always write it. The js-scroll mechanism emits no such StylesheetChange; its generated handler short-circuits on `matchMedia` instead (see `respectsReducedMotion` below). When `scriptChanges` is present, the diff carries a declarative `ScriptBehaviorChange` (the only one in v1 is `behavior: "parallax-scroll"`); it does NOT contain literal JS. Author an idempotent scroll handler from `descriptor` + `params` in the module that owns `sourceFile` (e.g. a `useEffect` keyed by `targetSelector`). The handler MUST batch updates with `requestAnimationFrame` (`params.throttle: "raf"`) and MUST short-circuit when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` (`respectsReducedMotion`); re-application replaces the prior handler rather than stacking listeners. CRITICAL: attach the scroll listener to `params.scrollSource` — `"window"` for page/viewport scroll, otherwise the CSS selector of the scroll container (an inner overlay or `<main>` that scrolls while `body` does not). Do NOT assume `window`; a window listener never fires for a nested scroll container, so the effect would be dead. Compute the offset from that source’s scroll position. The pure-CSS `scroll-driven` mechanism encodes the same choice in its `animation-timeline` (`scroll(root)` for the page vs `scroll()` for the nearest container) inside the StylesheetChange. Reject any `behavior` value other than `"parallax-scroll"`. Optionally filter by tab session ID. The `batches` index groups pending diffs by logical Apply-Changes click: `[{ batchId, batchNote?, createdAt, diffCount }]`, newest-first. Diffs without a `batchId` (legacy) are omitted from `batches` but appear in `changes`. Pass `batchId` to filter `changes` to a single batch. Use `get_queue_status.latest_batch_id` to identify the most recently submitted batch.

tabId.description: Optional tab session ID to filter by

batchId.description: Optional batch ID to filter changes to a single batch

name: get_project_components
description: Returns the project's discovered local React components (JSX/TSX) — each entry includes componentName, workspace-relative importPath, exportType (named or default), and props ([] in v1; prop schema is reserved for v1.1). Components are discovered from convention-gated roots (src/components, src/ui, components — overridable via nco-web-editor.componentRoots in the target project package.json). Optionally filter by a case-insensitive substring of componentName. Used to resolve InsertChange.componentInsert descriptors emitted by the extension into source-level JSX usages + imports.

name: get_queue_status
description: Returns lightweight queue status: active/closed, pending count, last update timestamp, and `latest_batch_id` (the batchId of the most recently ingested batch — absent until the first batch arrives). Use this instead of get_pending_visual_changes when you only need to check whether diffs are waiting or to identify the most recent batch.

name: get_token_drift_report
description: Returns a session-scoped report of custom value usage — values that did not match any design token.

name: import_session
description: Loads a previously exported session file into the pending queue.

inputPath.description: Path to the session export JSON file

name: reject_visual_change
description: Marks a visual diff as rejected and removes it from the pending queue.

diffId.description: The unique ID of the diff to reject

name: resolve_to_token
description: Maps a CSS value to the nearest design token for a given property.
